subject.title: [Bug] QQ Bot: skill_workshop approval "Allow" button always recorded as rejected

question: For QQ Bot C2C approval buttons, must authorization bind the callback actor to the original approval recipient or configured owner, or may direct-chat type alone grant approval authority?
rationale: OpenClaw's documented open-DM mode permits any sender, so the linked PR's assumption that every C2C conversation is inherently owner-only cannot be accepted safely without an explicit authorization decision.

options.title: Bind callback identity
options.body: Require the callback actor, QQ account, and C2C target to match the original approval recipient or configured owner before resolving the approval.

options.title: Require explicit approvers
options.body: Keep command-style explicit authorization for all approval callbacks and improve setup or diagnostics for direct-chat users without an owner entry.

options.title: Trust direct chat type
options.body: Allow every C2C callback to resolve approvals, accepting that public-DM configurations may grant approval authority to non-owner senders.

recommendation.title: Bind callback identity
recommendation.body: Require the callback actor, QQ account, and C2C target to match the original approval recipient or configured owner before resolving the approval.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent QQ Bot authorization hardening makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the security-boundary choice.
